resources.string: You can\'t cover the minimum bet. Reset to %1$d chips? Your statistics are kept.
Your saved round couldn\'t be opened. It was cancelled and no chips were lost.
Get a hand worth more than the dealer\'s without going over 21. If you go over, you bust and lose at once.

You start with 1,000 chips. Chips are for play only and cannot be bought or cashed out. Bets go in steps of 10, from 10 up to 500. If you run out of chips you can reset to 1,000, and your statistics are kept.

Number cards count their number. Jack, Queen and King count 10. An Ace counts 1 or 11, whichever is better for the hand. An Ace with a ten-value card on your first two cards is Blackjack, and pays 3 to 2.

Place your bet and press Deal. You and the dealer each get two cards, and one of the dealer\'s stays face down. You then make your decisions, one hand at a time, and when you are done the dealer plays. Every round is dealt from a fresh shuffle, and there is no undo.
Take one more card. You can keep hitting as long as your hand is under 21.
Keep your hand as it is and end your turn.
On your first two cards, double your bet and take exactly one more card. Your turn then ends. Use it when your hand is strong but not finished yet.
When your first two cards have the same rank, split them into two hands, each with the original bet. You can have up to four hands in all. Split Aces get one card each and cannot be hit again.
When the dealer shows an Ace, you may insure for half your bet. It pays 2 to 1 if the dealer has Blackjack, and is lost if not.
The dealer makes no choices: they take cards until they have 17 or more, and stand on every 17, including a soft 17 that counts an Ace as 11.
A simple plan that gives you good odds. The Hint button follows the same strategy in full detail.
Always hit a total of 8 or less, and always stand on a hard 17 or more.
With 12 to 16, stand if the dealer shows 2 to 6, because the dealer is likely to bust. Hit if the dealer shows 7 or higher.
Double on 11, and on 10 when the dealer shows 9 or less. If you cannot double, hit.
Always split Aces and 8s. Never split 5s or 10s; play them as 10 and 20.
With an Ace counting as 11 (a soft hand), hit up to soft 17 and stand on soft 19 or more.
Never take insurance. Over time it costs more than it pays back.
Strategy lowers the house\'s edge but cannot promise a win: the dealer\'s hidden card still decides many rounds.
